*   **What is the average cost of Facebook advertising?**  
    Facebook ads generally cost around $0.30 – $4.00 per click (CPC) and $3 – $20 per 1,000 impressions (CPM), with costs varying based on campaign objective, bidding strategy, and ad quality.
*   **How much should businesses spend on Facebook ads monthly?**  
    Most businesses spend $1.00 – $500.00 per month on Facebook ads (63% of respondents), though some companies allocate $3,000+ monthly depending on their advertising budget and campaign goals.
*   **What percentage of ad budgets goes to Facebook advertising?**  
    Most businesses allocate 0 – 15% of their total advertising budget to Facebook ads (53% of respondents), with the exact percentage depending on company goals and the ROI received from Facebook campaigns.
*   **Is Facebook advertising worth the investment?**  
    More than 80% of businesses report that advertising on Facebook is worth the cost and are satisfied with their return on investment, making it an effective platform for most companies due to its reach and targeting capabilities.
*   **What is the minimum budget to start Facebook advertising?**  
    The absolute minimum spend is $1 per day, though testing campaigns effectively requires at least $5 per day for 6-7 days to allow Meta’s algorithm to optimize ad delivery and provide meaningful performance data.

## How much do Facebook ads cost?

Facebook ads generally cost around $0.30 – $4.00 per click (CPC) and $3 – $20 per 1,000 impressions (CPM). Your actual Facebook ad cost depends on your campaign objective, bidding strategy, ad quality, and the conversion data Meta’s automated delivery has to work with.

Many advertisers start by testing at $1 – $5 per day, then set a monthly budget once they know what each lead or sale costs. Monthly spend varies widely by goals, industry, and audience targeting.

## Typical Facebook ad costs by metric

So, now that you know the answer to the question “how much does it cost to advertise on Facebook,” let’s look at costs by metrics.

The cost of Facebook ads will vary depending on the goal and objective of your campaign. Let’s take a look at Facebook advertising costs for the most common metrics:

*   **CPC (Cost Per click):** CPC can range between $0.30 – $4.00 depending on the industry and season. The average value for businesses is around $0.80.
*   **CPM (Cost Per 1,000 Impressions):** CPM can cost anywhere from $3 to $20, with the average sitting around $8.
*   **CPL (Cost Per Lead):** CPL can vary widely depending on your industry, and can typically range from $8  to $25, but can be much higher for some business-to-business (B2B) companies.
*   **CPA (Cost Per Action):** CPA can range from $8 to $55 and can also depend on you industry and the time of year.

Facebook Ads on a Budget: What £5–£50 a Day Gets You (UK)

[Insights](https://bonsandfrazer.com/insights/)/Meta Ads

# Facebook Ads on a Budget: How to Make £5-£50 a Day Actually Work

How much should a UK small business spend on Facebook ads? Real daily budgets, what each level can achieve, and when £5 a day is simply wasted money.

![](https://bonsandfrazer.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/jamie-frazer-bons-frazer.webp) By [Jamie Frazer](https://bonsandfrazer.com/#team) 11 June 2026 23 min read

![The Roll Safe meme: a man tapping his temple with a knowing grin](https://bonsandfrazer.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/facebook-ads-on-a-budget.jpg)

A small-budget playbook – for businesses spending £5-£50 a day, not £500. If you’re weighing Meta against Google first, read [Google Ads vs Facebook Ads](https://bonsandfrazer.com/insights/google-ads-vs-facebook-ads/); this guide assumes you’ve decided to run Meta. For the full strategy beyond budget, see our [Facebook ads for small business](https://bonsandfrazer.com/insights/facebook-ads-for-small-business/) guide.

**“Facebook ads” and “Meta ads” are the same thing.** It's Meta's ad platform, running across Facebook, Instagram, Messenger and the Audience Network — not just Facebook. We say “Facebook ads” throughout because that's what most people call it.

Most advice on running Facebook ads comes from people who either don’t run ads at all, or only manage accounts spending £500+ a day. Neither is any use to you if you’re working with £15 a day. **A small budget isn’t a smaller version of a big budget – it’s a different game, and it has to be played differently.**

The good news: small budgets absolutely work on Meta. The bad news: the platform’s defaults and most of YouTube’s advice will quietly waste yours. Here’s how to run **Facebook ads on a budget** properly – the campaign structure, the objective, the offer, the creative, and the mistakes that sink most small accounts.

**How much should a small business spend on Facebook ads?**  
For a UK small business generating leads, a workable starting budget is **£12-£25 a day (roughly £360-£750 a month)**. Below about £10 a day you can still get enquiries, but so few that costs swing week to week and you can’t tell a good ad from a lucky one. At £5 a day, treat it as a test of your offer and creative, not a lead engine.

## What does each daily budget actually get you?

These figures assume a cost per lead of around **£20**, which is in the range we commonly see for UK local service businesses using lead forms. Treat it as an illustration, not a benchmark: your own cost per lead depends on your trade, area, offer and creative. Halve the lead numbers if your cost per lead is £40; double them at £10.

| Daily budget | Monthly (approx.) | Leads a week at £20 CPL | Exits learning phase? | What it’s good for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| £5  | £150 | 1-2 | No  | Testing whether an offer or ad gets any response at all |
| £12-£25 | £360-£750 | 4-8 | No  | The realistic range for predictable monthly lead flow |
| £30-£50 | £900-£1,500 | 10-17 | No, not on leads | Room to test several ads at once and scale what works |
| £140+ | £4,200+ | About 50 | Yes | What it takes to exit learning on leads at £20 each |

**The part most guides skip:** at £20 a lead, you’d need around £1,000 a week (roughly £140 a day) to hit Meta’s ~50 conversions a week. Almost no small business spends that, so almost every small-budget account runs “Learning Limited”. That’s fine. It just means you keep the structure simple: one campaign, one ad set, and don’t touch it for a week. The sections below cover how to do that.

## Can you actually run Facebook ads on a small budget?

Yes. Meta has no minimum monthly spend, only a small daily floor per ad set, so you can start from a few pounds a day – and its low barrier and precise targeting make it genuinely accessible to small businesses. The catch: a small budget must be run differently to a big one. Spread it thin and you’ll learn nothing; concentrate it and you’ll learn fast.

The reason small budgets can work at all is that Meta is a discovery platform: it shows your ad to people whose behaviour suggests they’ll care, before they go looking. You don’t need a five-figure budget to tap into that. What you do need is the discipline to run a focused campaign – because on a small budget, every wasted pound is a much bigger share of your data.

## What is the minimum daily budget for Facebook ads in 2026?

**Meta’s own floor is tiny:** about **$1 a day per ad set** if you’re charged per impression, about **$5 a day** if you’re charged per click, like or video view, and around **$40 a day** for rare events like app installs or offer claims. UK accounts see the pound equivalent in Ads Manager. That’s the least Meta will accept, not the least that works. For lead generation, the working floor is nearer **£10-£12 a day**.

People searching “Meta minimum daily budget” usually want one of two numbers. The first is the figure Ads Manager will let you save. The second is the figure that actually produces enquiries. They’re very different.

|     | Meta’s technical minimum | Working minimum for UK lead gen |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Per ad set, per day | About $1-$5 (pound equivalent shown in Ads Manager) | £10-£12 |
| Per month | Well under £150 | £300-£360 |
| What it gets you | Delivery. Your ad runs, to very few people | 3-4 leads a week at a £20 cost per lead |
| Can you judge the ad? | No. Too little data to tell good from lucky | Yes, after three to four weeks |

**Three rules matter more than Meta’s floor:**

1.  **The minimum applies to each ad set.** If you set budgets at ad-set level, every ad set has to clear the floor on its own. Four ad sets means four floors, and four slices of an already small budget. It’s one more reason to [run one ad set](https://bonsandfrazer.com/insights/facebook-ads-on-a-budget/#structure).
2.  **Your cost per lead sets the real floor.** Our rule of thumb: spend at least half your expected cost per lead each day, so you average a lead every couple of days. At £20 a lead, that’s £10 a day. At £40 a lead (common in competitive trades), it’s £20.
3.  **A daily budget is an average, not a cap.** Meta can spend more than your daily figure on a strong day and less on a weak one, but it balances out across the week. [How Meta paces your budget](https://bonsandfrazer.com/insights/facebook-ads-on-a-budget/#budget) covers the detail.

The same floor applies to Instagram ads, because Facebook and Instagram ads are bought through the same Ads Manager and share one budget. Meta does change these figures from time to time, and they vary by currency. The number Ads Manager shows when you save the ad set is the one that counts. Source: Meta Business Help Centre, [Best practices for minimum budgets](https://en-gb.facebook.com/business/help/203183363050448).
